name: Saltbone Larder — the Gray Zone Street Kitchen
creator: Ogechi Tran-Kowalczyk
description: A legendary cart-turned-permanent-stall operating under the Ashburn overpass since 2191, Saltbone Larder built its reputation on 'bone broth extensions' — synth-protein bases slow-cooked with salvaged real marrow bones rented by the hour from a cooperative bone broker. The menu rotates daily but always features Ogechi's signature Nkwobi-Pho, a fusion of Igbo spiced offal and Vietnamese bone broth technique that costs Φ3.80 and has a two-hour queue by 07:00. Physical chalk menus only — no neural feed presence by deliberate choice.
cultural_impact: Saltbone Larder became a touchstone of the Gray Zone food identity, proving that real-ingredient cooking could survive below Tier 3 through communal resource-sharing models that other cart operators began to replicate across the corridor.
controversy: Ogechi was twice cited by HelixCorp Health Compliance for operating unlicensed bone-handling equipment; both citations were dropped after the Gray Zone community protests blocked a HelixCorp distribution route for six hours.
story_hooks: The bone broker cooperative that supplies Saltbone Larder is discovered to be fronting a gray-market organ preservation network — and Ogechi may or may not know.
A Tier 4 food journalist's neural-feed exposé on Saltbone Larder goes viral in the Spire, causing a tourist influx that threatens to price out the Gray Zone regulars who kept it alive.
Someone has started poisoning the broth stock — targeted, surgical, leaving no trace — and only Ogechi's regulars are getting sick.
